text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bardhyl Kokalari, former ambassador to Sweden, asked the Swedish government for political asylum. In 1994, Kokalari came under attack from Albania's media for writing a letter against writer Ismail Kadare, candidate for the Nobel prize.
- Ruling Democratic party removed Azem Hajdari, one of the party's founders, from its parlimentary group for opposing the party's policies.
- The Albanian Helsinki Committee says its staff are not being given access to prisoners complaining of ill treatment.
- Some 700 homes in the southern district of Berat were slightly damaged by an earthquake last Sunday.
- A German soccer association official will visit Albania to check accomodation, the soccer stadium and telecommunication arrangements before the World Cup group nine qualifier in April.
- Pyramid scheme companies say they will take their capital out of banks if they fail to give them more than 30 million leks a day.
- The opposition Socialist party accuses the ruling Democrats of creating a deep political, institutional, economic and financial crisis in the country.
